title: Supersede stale active Work Item safely
outOfScope: Changing a Provider pull request, merging a dependency update, publishing a release, or modifying immutable archived evidence.
Deleting any worktree or branch whose active identity and replacement evidence are not explicitly assessed by this Work Item.
Treating a locally present old branch as proof that its active Contract is current or ready for merge.

sources.reason: Current start gate only inspects active Contracts in the invoking worktree, so a stale active Contract in another linked worktree does not block a duplicate Work Item.
Owns lifecycle start and archive regressions for linked worktree behavior.
Authoritative English lifecycle guidance must explain the repository-wide active Work Item invariant and supersession recovery boundary.
Authoritative Japanese lifecycle guidance must preserve the same boundary for Japanese installation engineers.
Records the discovered duplicate active #441 Work Item as a release-blocking process finding.

rawUserRequest: When stale local worktrees or branches remain, converge them; do not leave latent hazards. If a process problem is found, fix it in the skill and executable checks before continuing the next Work Item. Continue the authorized plan without unnecessary pauses.

riskAssessment.reason: A stale active Contract in another linked worktree can allow duplicate delivery, leave unreviewed local changes, and make a later cleanup destroy evidence without a verifiable replacement relationship.

executionDecision.reason: The user has authorized continuous correction of discovered process defects before the next release prerequisite.

preReviewWarnings: The new guard must inspect linked worktrees without treating arbitrary untracked directories or detached historical worktrees as active Work Items.
The guard must block a new start before it writes its own Contract or Status, and its diagnostic must identify the conflicting worktree and Work Item ID.
The corrective must preserve the immutable archived #441 replacement evidence and only record a cleanup decision for the stale local predecessor.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: A1: ai-start rejects a new Work Item when a different linked worktree contains a valid active Contract/Summary pair, before it creates a new Contract, Summary, Start Receipt, or generated Status.
A2: the diagnostic names the conflicting linked worktree path, branch, and Work Item ID; a detached worktree or an active pair in the invoking worktree retains existing behavior.
A3: focused regressions cover the conflict, no-conflict, malformed-pair, detached, and no-partial-write cases without depending on the developer machine's actual worktree list.

A4: English and Japanese repository workflow references state that a replacement delivery does not silently retire another active Work Item; it must be assessed, recorded, and cleaned only after replacement evidence is preserved.

A5: the Summary records the stale dependabot-441-setup-dotnet-20260729 discovery, its replacement PR #468/archive evidence, and the exact post-closure cleanup boundary without changing either historical evidence set.
A6: focused tests, all Contract checks, full quality, archive, aggregate PR verification, Hosted CI, merge, closure, and branch cleanup complete before Dependabot #444 begins.
guidelines: Preserve fail-closed serial Work Item behavior; an unresolved linked active pair must block rather than be ignored.
Use test-driven development: add the linked-worktree failure regression before production behavior.
Do not delete or mutate the stale Work Item from the guard; the guard only identifies and blocks it.
Keep English and Japanese workflow statements semantically aligned.
Record the #441 replacement relationship as evidence, not as a claim that the stale branch was safely closed.

intent.problem: The original dependabot-441-setup-dotnet-20260729 Work Item remains active on an obsolete local branch even though the same dependency update was later delivered by archived Work Item dependabot-441-setup-dotnet-20260730 and merged as PR #468. ai-start only checks the invoking worktree, so it did not prevent this duplicate active identity from remaining as a latent cleanup and delivery hazard.
constraints: Do not rewrite the archived replacement evidence, reopen Dependabot #441, or merge the stale branch.
Do not delete the user-owned top-level worktree or discard its generated current_status change.
Detect only linked Git worktrees with a valid active Contract/Summary pair; malformed pairs remain fail-closed diagnostics.
The check must run before ai-start writes any new lifecycle files.
intent.rationale: Repository-wide serial execution requires an active Work Item to be unique across all linked worktrees, not merely within the current directory. An early deterministic guard prevents duplicate implementation and forces an evidence-backed supersession/cleanup decision.

declaredIntent.summary: Enforce repository-wide uniqueness of active Work Items across linked worktrees and record the discovered stale #441 predecessor without rewriting history.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A different linked worktree contains a valid active Work Item pair.
scenarioCoverage.expected: ai-start fails before any current-worktree lifecycle write and names the conflicting path, branch, and Work Item ID.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Create temporary linked-worktree fixture metadata and assert the start transaction has no Contract, Summary, Start Receipt, or Status writes.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: No other linked worktree has an active pair, or a historical worktree is detached.
scenarioCoverage.expected: ai-start retains existing dedicated-branch behavior and does not report a false conflict.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add isolated unit cases for no conflict and detached worktree entries.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Another worktree has a malformed single active file.
scenarioCoverage.expected: ai-start fails closed with a malformed-active diagnostic rather than silently ignoring the record.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add a mutation case with only a Contract or only a Summary in the linked worktree.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: The user authorized process corrections, executable checks, and convergence of stale worktrees before continuing the release plan.
